# Bargain Search — Spec

Status: ready-for-agent
Date: 2026-10-23

## Summary

A chat-authored buying intent that fans out keyword searches across marketplaces, then enriches the surfaced listings with AI-extracted facts (product identity, condition, bundle contents) so the user sees a curated, annotated view instead of raw keyword matches. The enhanced view is the product; the raw keyword page remains as the control group.

Terminology is canonical in `GLOSSARY.md`: **Bargain Search**, **Enrichment**, **Deal Target** (avoid — use Bargain Search), **Authored description**, **Unidentified listing**.

## Flow

1. **Chat authors the Bargain Search.** User talks to the LLM (halogen flash-next) about what they want to buy. The LLM asks clarifying questions until it can state the product identity back to the user, then presents a draft: a human-readable summary line ("Core i5-8400 mini PCs, complete, ≤ $150"), the curated keyword query list, and any exclusions. The user confirms or edits. Confirmation creates the Bargain Search. The user trusts the LLM to translate the summary into keyword queries; the summary is the human-auditable artifact, not the query list.
2. **Fan-out.** All curated queries run across eBay, OfferUp, and Facebook Marketplace (paginated), merged, deduped by (marketplace, listing id). Tolerant of any single marketplace failing — a zero from FB is a note, not an error. Same tolerance pattern as existing `_search_all`.
3. **Triage (small model).** Every new listing gets a cheap pass: title + snippet judged against the Bargain Search's product identity → **match / not-match / unsure**. Not-matches stay in the pass-through view but never enter the enhanced view. Unsures stay visible with a "needs review" marker — never silently dropped.
4. **Enrichment (large model).** Listings marked match or unsure are queued for the big model. It reads the full listing text (detail fetch, see below) and extracts strict field values: resolved product (manufacturer / model / config), condition (from the fixed set), bundle contents (each extra a product), with per-field confidence. A field the model can't fill is `unknown`, rendered as "?" — never guessed. Low-confidence fields explicitly invite an authored description.
5. **Enhanced view.** Matches only by default, ✨ on enriched cards, "show all" toggle as the safety net, reject button on enriched cards. Reject feeds the Bargain Search's exclusion list ("not this: OptiPlex 3070"); the next triage pass respects it. Authored description always overrides AI enrichment.

## Bargain Search lifecycle

- Multiple concurrent Bargain Searches.
- One-shot in MVP with a manual **re-run** button. Scheduled auto-rerun (Watch behavior) is deferred.
- **Refinement mutates the existing Bargain Search with a version bump.** The user hops into the chat at any time; the LLM translates the new needs into new knob positions (queries, filters, target price). Old results stay tagged with the version that found them.
- Target price is a field on the Bargain Search, editable via chat or directly. It is an **optional filter**: the enhanced view shows all matches by default; the user turns on the price filter when they have a number in mind. `shortcut: MVP treats asking price as out-the-door price; upgrade when per-marketplace shipping/fee parsing is reliable.`

## Data model (SQLite, single file, stdlib sqlite3, no ORM)

- `bargain_searches`: id, summary, product_identity, target_price, queries (json), exclusions (json), version, status, created_at, updated_at
- `conversations`: bargain_search_id, role, content, created_at — full chat transcript, append-only
- `listings`: id (`marketplace:listing_id`), raw fields (json), first_seen_at
- `enrichments`: listing_id, product (json), condition, bundle (json), confidence (json), model, status (`pending` / `enriched` / `failed`), created_at
- `rejects`: bargain_search_id, listing_id, reason, created_at

Enrichment is keyed by listing, not by Bargain Search: intrinsic facts about a listing are cached once, forever. Relevance judgment is per (listing, Bargain Search) and is cheap to re-run. A new Bargain Search next month = fresh triage over cached listings, zero big-model re-calls for already-enriched ones.

## Model contract (boldhalo router)

- OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, model name passed per call. boldtrader does not care which model answers; boldhalo owns routing.
- **Chat + enrichment**: `qwen3.8-flash-next-w4b-q8-halogen` (user's loaded model, liked).
- **Triage**: `decider-0.8b` on the XDNA 2 NPU via halogen's `/classify` endpoint (zero GPU memory). Fallback if NPU path unavailable: CPU-only Qwen3-4B-class Q4_K_M.
- Enrichment output contract: fixed schema, short field values, explicit `unknown` per field. The schema is boldtrader's; the model fills slots and never shapes the record. A bad field degrades to "?" instead of breaking the parse.
- Full stack rationale, hardware facts, and verify-first list: `docs/research/local-models-ms-s1-max.md`. Port the requirements into boldhalo from there.

## Orchestration

No framework. The pipeline is linear (fan-out → triage → enrichment), single-machine, and resumability is already handled by status columns in SQLite: a plain worker loop that picks `pending` rows, calls the router, writes results, retries once on failure. Airflow is overkill; Celery/RQ/Dramatiq all require a Redis broker and worker supervision to solve problems we don't have yet (distributed scheduling, fan-out across machines, DAG dependencies). The queue *is* the database. Revisit only if we outgrow one worker or need cron-style scheduled re-runs — at that point Huey (SQLite-backed, no broker) is the lightest step up.

## New marketplace interface

`Marketplace` gains `fetch_detail(listing) -> ListingDetail`: full description text, images, shipping/fee fields where the marketplace exposes them. Per-marketplace implementation:

- eBay: public listing page, trivial.
- OfferUp: GraphQL detail query — verify anonymous access before committing.
- Facebook: via the existing Playwright path; best-effort.

If a marketplace's detail fetch is unreliable, its listings get small-model triage only and are marked "enrichment unavailable" — one marketplace never blocks the pipeline.

## UI

- **Bargain Search list page** (new home): one row per search — summary line, status (running 34/120 · complete), match count, last-run time. Click → enhanced view. "New bargain search" launches chat.
- **Enhanced view**: match-filtered cards with ✨ enrichment annotations, pending markers on un-enriched listings, show-all toggle, reject button per card, target-price filter.
- **Chat panel**: create and refine; transcript persisted with the search.
- **Raw keyword search**: the existing page, unchanged, linked from the header as the control group.

## Performance expectations (from research)

- Triage: ~500 listings under a minute on NPU.
- Enrichment: ~30–60 s per listing → a 100-listing Bargain Search fills over ~1–2 hours. This is by design: kick it off, hunt manually, check back as results stream in.
- Enrichment concurrency 1 so chat never queues behind a batch on the same GPU. Queue persisted; server restart resumes it. Failed enrichment retries once, then marks failed.

## MVP scope

**In:** chat authoring + confirmation, fan-out, NPU triage, big-model enrichment with detail fetch, enhanced view (filter, toggle, ✨, reject), target-price filter, SQLite persistence, re-run.

**Deferred:** fair-price / deal-threshold machinery and price-observation accumulation (ADR 0001/0004), auto-rerunning Watches, vision on listing photos, correction-feedback learning, per-marketplace out-the-door fee extraction.

## Verification

Before trusting the stack (order per research doc): halogen startup "host memory left" line → NPU/fabric-clock gate → decider accuracy vs a human-labeled sample of ~50 listings → concurrent NPU+GPU decode interference → sustained thermals. Then: enrichment JSON reliability on 20 real listings across the three marketplaces before wiring the full enhanced view.

1:# BoldTrader
2:
3:Finds deals on used computer hardware across online marketplaces. Scope is used goods only: secondhand, refurbished, for-parts, and damaged listings. New retail is out of scope.
4:
5:## Language
6:
7:**Deal**:
8:A listing whose effective price falls meaningfully below the fair price for that product in that condition.
9:_Avoid_: bargain (except in "Bargain Search"), steal, sale
10:
11:**Flip value**:
12:The resale value of components included in a listing that the buyer does not need. Subtracted from the out-the-door price to get the effective price. A bundle of unwanted extras can turn an overpriced listing into a deal.
13:_Avoid_: salvage value, resale value (of the wanted item)
14:
15:**Effective price**:
16:What the buyer really pays for the thing they want: out-the-door price minus the flip value of unwanted bundled components. The number deal math compares against fair price.
17:_Avoid_: net price, real cost
18:
19:**Bundle**:
20:A single listing that includes multiple things — the wanted product plus extra components, each extra itself a Product with its own identity. Flip value applies to the unwanted extras.
21:_Avoid_: lot, package, set
22:
23:**Fair price**:
24:An estimate of what a given product in a given condition typically goes for, derived from our own recorded price observations over time. Fair price is a function of both product and condition, never the product alone. It does not depend on any marketplace exposing sold history.
25:_Avoid_: market price, real price
26:
27:**Price observation**:
28:A single recorded data point: the effective price seen for a product in a given condition on a given day. The pricing database is built by accumulating these observations over time.
29:_Avoid_: price point, data point
30:
31:**Product**:
32:The canonical thing a listing is selling, identified by the app from the listing's own data (model numbers, specs), or by a user-authored description when the listing is too poorly described to parse automatically. Not from a user-maintained catalog. Price observations are pooled per product.
33:_Avoid_: item, SKU, catalog entry
34:
35:**Unidentified listing**:
36:A listing the app cannot resolve to a product — typically vague titles, missing model numbers, poor photos. Surfaced in a separate bucket rather than dropped; these often hide the best deals precisely because they're poorly described. Resolved by a user-authored description (see Grandma search).
37:_Avoid_: unmatched, failed listing
38:
39:**Grandma search**:
40:Searching with plain, layperson terms ("good computer", "CPU tower") rather than model numbers, to surface listings from sellers who don't know what they have. When such a listing is found, the user authors their own description from the listing photos and direct conversation with the seller.
41:_Avoid_: naive search, fuzzy search
42:
43:**Authored description**:
44:A description the user writes for a listing based on what they see in the photos and learn from direct conversation with the seller. Used to resolve a poorly-described listing into a known product and condition.
45:_Avoid_: user note, manual description
46:
47:**Condition**:
48:The state of the specific thing in a listing, drawn from a fixed set: complete, cosmetic damage, missing parts, for parts, refurbished. Condition changes the fair price; it is not merely a filter. Provenance varies by marketplace: eBay exposes structured condition IDs, Facebook exposes coarse used-grades, OfferUp exposes free text only on the detail record. Where structured values exist they map into the canonical set rather than passing through; where absent, condition is inferred from listing text or from the user's authored description. Neither provenance is fully trustworthy — sellers mislabel.
49:_Avoid_: state, grade, quality
50:
51:**Refurbished**:
52:A condition: professionally restored and tested, typically with a warranty. Its fair price includes the value of that restoration and sits apart from plain complete.
53:_Avoid_: reconditioned, renewed
54:
55:**Asking price**:
56:The price a seller posted on a listing. The number deal math uses for comparison. Negotiation is possible on every marketplace; on some it is expected and the ask runs systematically above the eventual transaction price, but the app treats the ask as the comparison number regardless.
57:_Avoid_: listed price, price
58:
59:**Out-the-door price**:
60:What the buyer actually pays: asking price plus shipping plus any fees. The number deal math compares against fair price.
61:_Avoid_: total, sticker price
62:
63:**Listing**:
64:One seller's posting of one thing on one marketplace. The atomic unit of supply.
65:_Avoid_: item, offer, posting
66:
67:**Search**:
68:A keyword query submitted to a marketplace, returning a paginated set of Listings. Ephemeral by default — a Search becomes durable only when saved as a Watch.
69:_Avoid_: query, filter
70:
71:**Watch**:
72:A saved search the user tracks. The app surfaces new listings matching a watch.
73:_Avoid_: alert, saved search, tracker
74:
75:**Locality**:
76:The geographic scope of a watch: a center point and a radius. Local marketplaces are metro-scoped — a watch without a locality on a local marketplace sees nothing useful.
77:_Avoid_: area, region, location
78:
79:**Deal threshold**:
80:How far below fair price a listing must fall to count as a deal, expressed as a percentage. A global default applies to every product; the user may override it per product. Market analysis may raise the threshold where a product's observed prices are noisy, but never lower it below the floor.
81:_Avoid_: cutoff, margin
82:
83:**Price surge**:
84:A sustained rise in a product's market price driven by external events — new releases, component shortages, hype — rather than anything about individual listings. During a surge, listings priced at the surged level are not deals even if they look cheap against older memory.
85:_Avoid_: spike, inflation
86:
87:**Wave**:
88:A burst of supply into the used market, typically triggered by corporate decommissioning cycles. Deals cluster in waves; between waves, supply thins.
89:_Avoid_: glut, flood
90:
91:**Marketplace**:
92:A platform where listings appear — eBay, OfferUp, Facebook Marketplace, and similar. Marketplaces differ in what data they expose, their fee structures, whether they support bartering, and whether they offer a sanctioned API.
93:_Avoid_: platform, site, store
94:
95:**For parts**:
96:A condition in which the thing is sold broken or incomplete, priced for salvage rather than use. Its fair price derives from salvage value, not from working comps.
97:_Avoid_: broken, junk, scrap
98:
99:**ITAD** (IT Asset Disposition):
100:A business that acquires decommissioned enterprise equipment, wipes or destroys data, and resells it. A primary source of bulk used hardware.
101:_Avoid_: recycler, liquidator

# BoldTrader

Finds deals on used computer hardware across online marketplaces. Scope is used goods only: secondhand, refurbished, for-parts, and damaged listings. New retail is out of scope.

## Language

**Deal**:
A listing whose effective price falls meaningfully below the fair price for that product in that condition.
_Avoid_: bargain (except in "Bargain Search"), steal, sale

**Flip value**:
The resale value of components included in a listing that the buyer does not need. Subtracted from the out-the-door price to get the effective price. A bundle of unwanted extras can turn an overpriced listing into a deal.
_Avoid_: salvage value, resale value (of the wanted item)

**Effective price**:
What the buyer really pays for the thing they want: out-the-door price minus the flip value of unwanted bundled components. The number deal math compares against fair price.
_Avoid_: net price, real cost

**Bundle**:
A single listing that includes multiple things — the wanted product plus extra components, each extra itself a Product with its own identity. Flip value applies to the unwanted extras.
_Avoid_: lot, package, set

**Fair price**:
An estimate of what a given product in a given condition typically goes for, derived from our own recorded price observations over time. Fair price is a function of both product and condition, never the product alone. It does not depend on any marketplace exposing sold history.
_Avoid_: market price, real price

**Price observation**:
A single recorded data point: the effective price seen for a product in a given condition on a given day. The pricing database is built by accumulating these observations over time.
_Avoid_: price point, data point

**Product**:
The canonical thing a listing is selling, identified by the app from the listing's own data (model numbers, specs), or by a user-authored description when the listing is too poorly described to parse automatically. Not from a user-maintained catalog. Price observations are pooled per product.
_Avoid_: item, SKU, catalog entry

**Unidentified listing**:
A listing the app cannot resolve to a product — typically vague titles, missing model numbers, poor photos. Surfaced in a separate bucket rather than dropped; these often hide the best deals precisely because they're poorly described. Resolved by a user-authored description (see Grandma search).
_Avoid_: unmatched, failed listing

**Grandma search**:
Searching with plain, layperson terms ("good computer", "CPU tower") rather than model numbers, to surface listings from sellers who don't know what they have. When such a listing is found, the user authors their own description from the listing photos and direct conversation with the seller.
_Avoid_: naive search, fuzzy search

**Authored description**:
A description the user writes for a listing based on what they see in the photos and learn from direct conversation with the seller. Used to resolve a poorly-described listing into a known product and condition.
_Avoid_: user note, manual description

**Condition**:
The state of the specific thing in a listing, drawn from a fixed set: complete, cosmetic damage, missing parts, for parts, refurbished. Condition changes the fair price; it is not merely a filter. Provenance varies by marketplace: eBay exposes structured condition IDs, Facebook exposes coarse used-grades, OfferUp exposes free text only on the detail record. Where structured values exist they map into the canonical set rather than passing through; where absent, condition is inferred from listing text or from the user's authored description. Neither provenance is fully trustworthy — sellers mislabel.
_Avoid_: state, grade, quality

**Refurbished**:
A condition: professionally restored and tested, typically with a warranty. Its fair price includes the value of that restoration and sits apart from plain complete.
_Avoid_: reconditioned, renewed

**Out-the-door price**:
What the buyer actually pays: asking price plus shipping plus any fees. The number deal math compares against fair price.
_Avoid_: total, sticker price

**Listing**:
One seller's posting of one thing on one marketplace. The atomic unit of supply.
_Avoid_: item, offer, posting

**Search**:

**Watch**:

_Avoid_: alert, saved search, tracker

**Locality**:
The geographic scope of a watch: a center point and a radius. Local marketplaces are metro-scoped — a watch without a locality on a local marketplace sees nothing useful.

A description the user writes for a listing based on what they see in the photos and learn from direct conversation with the seller. Used to resolve a poorly-described listing into a known product and condition.
_Avoid_: user note, manual description

**Condition**:
The state of the specific thing in a listing, drawn from a fixed set: complete, cosmetic damage, missing parts, for parts, refurbished. Condition changes the fair price; it is not merely a filter. Provenance varies by marketplace: eBay exposes structured condition IDs, Facebook exposes coarse used-grades, OfferUp exposes free text only on the detail record. Where structured values exist they map into the canonical set rather than passing through; where absent, condition is inferred from listing text or from the user's authored description. Neither provenance is fully trustworthy — sellers mislabel.
_Avoid_: state, grade, quality

**Refurbished**:
A condition: professionally restored and tested, typically with a warranty. Its fair price includes the value of that restoration and sits apart from plain complete.
_Avoid_: reconditioned, renewed

**Asking price**:
The price a seller posted on a listing. The number deal math uses for comparison. Negotiation is possible on every marketplace; on some it is expected and the ask runs systematically above the eventual transaction price, but the app treats the ask as the comparison number regardless.
_Avoid_: listed price, price

**Out-the-door price**:
What the buyer actually pays: asking price plus shipping plus any fees. The number deal math compares against fair price.
_Avoid_: total, sticker price

**Listing**:
One seller's posting of one thing on one marketplace. The atomic unit of supply.
_Avoid_: item, offer, posting

**Search**:
A keyword query submitted to a marketplace, returning a paginated set of Listings. Ephemeral by default — a Search becomes durable only when saved as a Watch.
_Avoid_: query, filter

**Watch**:
A saved search the user tracks. The app surfaces new listings matching a watch.
_Avoid_: alert, saved search, tracker

**Locality**:
The geographic scope of a watch: a center point and a radius. Local marketplaces are metro-scoped — a watch without a locality on a local marketplace sees nothing useful.
_Avoid_: area, region, location

**Deal threshold**:
How far below fair price a listing must fall to count as a deal, expressed as a percentage. A global default applies to every product; the user may override it per product. Market analysis may raise the threshold where a product's observed prices are noisy, but never lower it below the floor.
_Avoid_: cutoff, margin

**Price surge**:
A sustained rise in a product's market price driven by external events — new releases, component shortages, hype — rather than anything about individual listings. During a surge, listings priced at the surged level are not deals even if they look cheap against older memory.
_Avoid_: spike, inflation

**Wave**:
A burst of supply into the used market, typically triggered by corporate decommissioning cycles. Deals cluster in waves; between waves, supply thins.
_Avoid_: glut, flood

**Marketplace**:
A platform where listings appear — eBay, OfferUp, Facebook Marketplace, and similar. Marketplaces differ in what data they expose, their fee structures, whether they support bartering, and whether they offer a sanctioned API.
_Avoid_: platform, site, store

**For parts**:
A condition in which the thing is sold broken or incomplete, priced for salvage rather than use. Its fair price derives from salvage value, not from working comps.
_Avoid_: broken, junk, scrap

**ITAD** (IT Asset Disposition):
A business that acquires decommissioned enterprise equipment, wipes or destroys data, and resells it. A primary source of bulk used hardware.
_Avoid_: recycler, liquidator

**Enrichment**:
The AI-extracted facts added to a Listing beyond what the marketplace exposes: resolved product identity, normalized condition, and the bundle's contents as a list of additional products. Enrichment is a first draft — the user's authored description always overrides it.
_Avoid_: AI analysis, scoring, enhancement

**Bargain Search**:
A durable buying intent authored through a chat conversation with an LLM: the product(s) the user wants, plus a set of keyword queries the LLM curates and fans out across marketplaces. The broad net that feeds Enrichment; precise filtering happens after enrichment, not before.
_Avoid_: deal search, advanced search, broadcast

# BoldTrader

Finds deals on used computer hardware across online marketplaces. Scope is used goods only: secondhand, refurbished, for-parts, and damaged listings. New retail is out of scope.

## Language

**Deal**:
A listing whose effective price falls meaningfully below the fair price for that product in that condition.
_Avoid_: bargain (except in "Bargain Search"), steal, sale

**Flip value**:
The resale value of components included in a listing that the buyer does not need. Subtracted from the out-the-door price to get the effective price. A bundle of unwanted extras can turn an overpriced listing into a deal.
_Avoid_: salvage value, resale value (of the wanted item)

**Effective price**:
What the buyer really pays for the thing they want: out-the-door price minus the flip value of unwanted bundled components. The number deal math compares against fair price.
_Avoid_: net price, real cost

**Bundle**:
A single listing that includes multiple things — the wanted product plus extra components, each extra itself a Product with its own identity. Flip value applies to the unwanted extras.
_Avoid_: lot, package, set

**Fair price**:
An estimate of what a given product in a given condition typically goes for, derived from our own recorded price observations over time. Fair price is a function of both product and condition, never the product alone. It does not depend on any marketplace exposing sold history.
_Avoid_: market price, real price

**Price observation**:
A single recorded data point: the effective price seen for a product in a given condition on a given day. The pricing database is built by accumulating these observations over time.
_Avoid_: price point, data point

**Product**:
The canonical thing a listing is selling, identified by the app from the listing's own data (model numbers, specs), or by a user-authored description when the listing is too poorly described to parse automatically. Not from a user-maintained catalog. Price observations are pooled per product.
_Avoid_: item, SKU, catalog entry

**Unidentified listing**:
A listing the app cannot resolve to a product — typically vague titles, missing model numbers, poor photos. Surfaced in a separate bucket rather than dropped; these often hide the best deals precisely because they're poorly described. Resolved by a user-authored description (see Grandma search).
_Avoid_: unmatched, failed listing

**Grandma search**:
Searching with plain, layperson terms ("good computer", "CPU tower") rather than model numbers, to surface listings from sellers who don't know what they have. When such a listing is found, the user authors their own description from the listing photos and direct conversation with the seller.
_Avoid_: naive search, fuzzy search

**Authored description**:
A description the user writes for a listing based on what they see in the photos and learn from direct conversation with the seller. Used to resolve a poorly-described listing into a known product and condition.
_Avoid_: user note, manual description

**Condition**:
The state of the specific thing in a listing, drawn from a fixed set: complete, cosmetic damage, missing parts, for parts, refurbished. Condition changes the fair price; it is not merely a filter. Provenance varies by marketplace: eBay exposes structured condition IDs, Facebook exposes coarse used-grades, OfferUp exposes free text only on the detail record. Where structured values exist they map into the canonical set rather than passing through; where absent, condition is inferred from listing text or from the user's authored description. Neither provenance is fully trustworthy — sellers mislabel.
_Avoid_: state, grade, quality

**Refurbished**:
A condition: professionally restored and tested, typically with a warranty. Its fair price includes the value of that restoration and sits apart from plain complete.
_Avoid_: reconditioned, renewed

**Asking price**:
The price a seller posted on a listing. The number deal math uses for comparison. Negotiation is possible on every marketplace; on some it is expected and the ask runs systematically above the eventual transaction price, but the app treats the ask as the comparison number regardless.
_Avoid_: listed price, price

**Out-the-door price**:
What the buyer actually pays: asking price plus shipping plus any fees. The number deal math compares against fair price.
_Avoid_: total, sticker price

**Listing**:
One seller's posting of one thing on one marketplace. The atomic unit of supply.
_Avoid_: item, offer, posting

**Search**:
A keyword query submitted to a marketplace, returning a paginated set of Listings. Ephemeral by default — a Search becomes durable only when saved as a Watch.
_Avoid_: query, filter

**Watch**:
A saved search the user tracks. The app surfaces new listings matching a watch.
_Avoid_: alert, saved search, tracker

**Locality**:
The geographic scope of a watch: a center point and a radius. Local marketplaces are metro-scoped — a watch without a locality on a local marketplace sees nothing useful.
_Avoid_: area, region, location

**Deal threshold**:
How far below fair price a listing must fall to count as a deal, expressed as a percentage. A global default applies to every product; the user may override it per product. Market analysis may raise the threshold where a product's observed prices are noisy, but never lower it below the floor.
_Avoid_: cutoff, margin

**Price surge**:
A sustained rise in a product's market price driven by external events — new releases, component shortages, hype — rather than anything about individual listings. During a surge, listings priced at the surged level are not deals even if they look cheap against older memory.
_Avoid_: spike, inflation

**Wave**:
A burst of supply into the used market, typically triggered by corporate decommissioning cycles. Deals cluster in waves; between waves, supply thins.
_Avoid_: glut, flood

**Marketplace**:
A platform where listings appear — eBay, OfferUp, Facebook Marketplace, and similar. Marketplaces differ in what data they expose, their fee structures, whether they support bartering, and whether they offer a sanctioned API.
_Avoid_: platform, site, store

**For parts**:
A condition in which the thing is sold broken or incomplete, priced for salvage rather than use. Its fair price derives from salvage value, not from working comps.
_Avoid_: broken, junk, scrap

**ITAD** (IT Asset Disposition):
A business that acquires decommissioned enterprise equipment, wipes or destroys data, and resells it. A primary source of bulk used hardware.
_Avoid_: recycler, liquidator

**Enrichment**:
The AI-extracted facts added to a Listing beyond what the marketplace exposes: resolved product identity, normalized condition, and the bundle's contents as a list of additional products. Enrichment is a first draft — the user's authored description always overrides it.
_Avoid_: AI analysis, scoring, enhancement

**Bargain Search**:
A durable buying intent authored through a chat conversation with an LLM: the product(s) the user wants, plus a set of keyword queries the LLM curates and fans out across marketplaces. The broad net that feeds Enrichment; precise filtering happens after enrichment, not before.
_Avoid_: deal search, advanced search, broadcast

"""Marketplace abstraction: the interface every marketplace integration implements."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Listing:
    """One seller's posting of one thing on one marketplace."""

    id: str
    title: str
    price: float | None = None
    condition: str | None = None
    sold_count: int | None = None
    image_url: str | None = None
    url: str = ""
    snippet: str | None = None
    marketplace: str = ""  # stamped by the server after fetch


@dataclass
class SearchResult:
    """One page of Listings returned by a Search."""

    listings: list[Listing] = field(default_factory=list)
    total_results: int = 0
    page: int = 1
    page_size: int = 50
    total_pages: int = 0  # 0 = derive from total_results/page_size

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.total_pages <= 0:
            if self.total_results <= 0:
                self.total_pages = 1
            else:
                self.total_pages = max(1, math.ceil(self.total_results / self.page_size))


class Marketplace(ABC):
    """A platform where listings appear. Implement search() per platform."""

    name: str = "unknown"

    @abstractmethod
    def search(self, query: str, page: int = 1, location: str | None = None) -> SearchResult:
        """Run a keyword Search and return one page of Listings.

        location is a human place name (city, ZIP, metro). Marketplaces that
        are geo-scoped (OfferUp) require it; keyword-only ones ignore it.
        """

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Listing:
    """One seller's posting of one thing on one marketplace."""

    id: str
    title: str
    price: float | None = None
    condition: str | None = None
    sold_count: int | None = None
    image_url: str | None = None
    url: str = ""
    snippet: str | None = None
    marketplace: str = ""  # stamped by the server after fetch


@dataclass
class SearchResult:
    """One page of Listings returned by a Search."""

    listings: list[Listing] = field(default_factory=list)
    total_results: int = 0
    page: int = 1
    page_size: int = 50
    total_pages: int = 0  # 0 = derive from total_results/page_size

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.total_pages <= 0:
            if self.total_results <= 0:
                self.total_pages = 1
            else:
                self.total_pages = max(1, math.ceil(self.total_results / self.page_size))


class Marketplace(ABC):
    """A platform where listings appear. Implement search() per platform."""

    name: str = "unknown"

    @abstractmethod
    def search(self, query: str, page: int = 1, location: str | None = None) -> SearchResult:
        """Run a keyword Search and return one page of Listings.

        location is a human place name (city, ZIP, metro). Marketplaces that
        are geo-scoped (OfferUp) require it; keyword-only ones ignore it.
        """

# Issue tracker: Local Markdown

Issues and specs for this repo live as markdown files in `.scratch/`.

## Conventions

- One feature per directory: `.scratch/<feature-slug>/`
- The spec is `.scratch/<feature-slug>/spec.md`
- Implementation issues are one file per ticket at `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01`, never a single combined tickets file
- Triage state is recorded as a `Status:` line near the top of each issue file (see `triage-labels.md` for the role strings)
- Comments and conversation history append to the bottom of the file under a `## Comments` heading

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a new file under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/` (creating the directory if needed).

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Read the file at the referenced path. The user will normally pass the path or the issue number directly.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a file with one **child** file per ticket.

- **Map**: `.scratch/<effort>/map.md` (the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body).
- **Child ticket**: `.scratch/<effort>/issues/NN-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01`, with the question in the body. A `Type:` line records the ticket type (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`); a `Status:` line records `claimed`/`resolved`.
- **Blocking**: a `Blocked by: NN, NN` line near the top. A ticket is unblocked when every file it lists is `resolved`.
- **Frontier**: scan `.scratch/<effort>/issues/` for files that are open, unblocked, and unclaimed; first by number wins.
- **Claim**: set `Status: claimed` and save before any work.
- **Resolve**: append the answer under an `## Answer` heading, set `Status: resolved`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far in `map.md`.
